exercises.title: Audit trigger: log every real grade change (inserted ⋈ deleted)
exercises.problemHtml:
Create trg_Enrolment_Audit (AFTER UPDATE on Enrolment) that writes one row into GradeAudit(sid, cid, old_grade, new_grade, changed_at, changed_by) for every enrolment whose grade really changed — including NULL → value — and nothing for updates that leave the grade as it was. Use SYSDATETIME() and SUSER_SNAME().

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • One INSERT … SELECT … FROM inserted i JOIN deleted d ON the key.
  • Compare NULL-safely: ISNULL(i.grade, -1) <> ISNULL(d.grade, -1).

-- solution.sql — YOUR answer for: Audit trigger: log every real grade change (inserted ⋈ deleted)
-- Bài làm CỦA BẠN. Run order / thứ tự chạy: setup.sql → solution.sql → check.sql
USE DBI202_CL;
GO
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER trg_Enrolment_Audit ON Enrolment
AFTER UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    INSERT INTO GradeAudit (sid, cid, old_grade, new_grade, changed_at, changed_by)
    SELECT i.sid, i.cid, d.grade, i.grade, SYSDATETIME(), SUSER_SNAME()
    FROM inserted i
    JOIN deleted d ON d.sid = i.sid AND d.cid = i.cid
    WHERE ISNULL(i.grade, -1) <> ISNULL(d.grade, -1);      -- only real changes, NULL-safe
END

exercises.title: INSTEAD OF DELETE: soft-delete projects
exercises.problemHtml:
Projects must never disappear (their work history in tblWorksOn would be lost). The setup adds tblProject.isActive BIT DEFAULT 1. Create trSoftDeleteProject — INSTEAD OF DELETE on tblProject — that sets isActive = 0 for the projects being deleted instead of deleting them.

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The in-browser grader runs PostgreSQL (WASM) in a SQL Server–like mode and can only check portable SQL; this task needs T-SQL that only a real SQL Server runs (stored procedures, functions, triggers, variables, TRY/CATCH, transactions…). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • INSTEAD OF DELETE: the original DELETE does not run; your trigger body runs instead.
  • Mark every row of deleted (multi-row DELETE).

CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER trSoftDeleteProject ON tblProject
INSTEAD OF DELETE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    UPDATE p SET isActive = 0                   -- keep the row (its tblWorksOn history stays valid)
    FROM tblProject p
    WHERE p.proNum IN (SELECT proNum FROM deleted);
END

exercises.title: Replace the cursor with one UPDATE
exercises.problemHtml:
The cursor of practice 7.5 raises salaries one employee at a time: for each employee of departments 1 and 2, +10% if their total working hours are ≥ 30, otherwise +5%, rounded to whole VND. Do the same job with one UPDATE statement.

FUHCompany schema (the course's sample database — full script in the FUHCompany.sql tab)
TableColumns (PK underlined, FK in italics)
tblEmployeeempSSN DECIMAL(18,0), empName NVARCHAR(50), empAddress NVARCHAR(100), empSalary DECIMAL(10,0), empSex CHAR(1) (F/M), empBirthdate DATE, depNum → tblDepartment, supervisorSSN → tblEmployee
tblDepartmentdepNum INT, depName NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE, mgrSSN → tblEmployee, mgrAssDate DATE

14 employees, 5 departments, 6 projects, 16 work assignments, 5 dependents. Names are Vietnamese with diacritics; text compares case-insensitively as on SQL Server.

Requirements

  • One UPDATE with a CASE and a correlated subquery for the hours (an employee on no project has 0 hours).
  • ROUND(…, 0). No cursor, no loop.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Một câu thay vì 2n câu: UPDATE theo tập là nguyên tử, dùng một kế hoạch và mất vài mili giây trong khi cursor phát một câu lệnh mỗi dòng. Chỉ dùng cursor khi mỗi dòng cần một hành động thật sự khác nhau.
